Player forecasts are well calibrated. On the holdout, predicted buckets landed within about 3 points of actual hit rates. The test used who actually played, so live forecasts will be slightly worse because inactives are unknown in advance.

Game lines show no edge. Closing spread MAE was 9.70 points vs 10.11 for our line, and the fitted weight on our line was about zero. Closing totals: 10.18 vs 10.61. So game sides default to pass.

Prop edges are unproven. Calibration shows the probabilities are honest. It does not show they beat DraftKings, because no historical prop lines were available to test against. The edges here are leads to price-check.

2026 holdout, all markets. Dots near the dashed line mean a forecast of X% hit about X% of the time. Bigger dots hold more forecasts.

Data gaps

  • Prop prices: ESPN's DraftKings feed gives lines and milestone levels but no prices. Moneyline, spread and total prices are real. Prop edges assume -110, and each pick shows a minimum acceptable price.
  • 2026 coverage: man/zone and coverage shells have no free 2026 feed. 2025 charting stands in, labeled every time, and flagged when a head coach changed. Coordinator changes are not tracked.
  • Alignment and routes: 2026 slot/wide alignment and routes run are paid data. Target side, depth and 2025 route targets stand in. Press rate, shadow rate, tackle-vs-edge win rate, and run-scheme splits are left out.
  • Under-pressure splits: team pressure rates are 2026 (PFR). Individual QB pressure splits are 2025. Blitz splits are 2026 (FTN).
  • Injury odds: P(plays) values are assumptions from status and practice, not fitted estimates.

nflverse supplied play-by-play, FTN charting, PFR advanced stats, NGS, snap counts, depth charts and rosters. ESPN supplied the schedule, injuries and DraftKings lines. NWS supplied forecasts.

These are estimates, and no selection is guaranteed. After the games, run review.py to score every forecast (Phase 15).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Olamide Zaccheaus (WR, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Joe Burrow and Michael Penix Jr.. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Chase Brown 15+ rushing yds (95%) + Drake London 25+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 86.7%, fair -652. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 81.3% vs 81.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Chase Brown 30+ rushing yds (80%) + Drake London 50+ receiving yds (75%) + Bijan Robinson 60+ rushing yds (71%). Joint estimate 42.4%, fair +136. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 32.3% vs 32.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Bijan Robinson 70+ rushing yds (61%) + Drake London 70+ receiving yds (58%) + Drew Sample 4+ receiving yds (53%). Joint estimate 19.7%, fair +407. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 13.3% vs 12.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Chase Brown 15+ rushing yds (95%) + Drake London 25+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 86.7%, fair -652. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 81.3% vs 81.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Chase Brown 30+ rushing yds (80%) + Drake London 50+ receiving yds (75%) + Bijan Robinson 60+ rushing yds (71%). Joint estimate 42.4%, fair +136. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 32.3% vs 32.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Bijan Robinson 70+ rushing yds (61%) + Drake London 70+ receiving yds (58%) + Drew Sample 4+ receiving yds (53%). Joint estimate 19.7%, fair +407. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 13.3% vs 12.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Jalen Travis (OT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Dak Prescott and Daniel Jones. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Javonte Williams 30+ rushing yds (91%) + Keenan Allen 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 82.9%, fair -486. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.6% vs 76.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Dak Prescott 200+ passing yds (80%) + Josh Downs 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Keenan Allen 20+ receiving yds (79%). Joint estimate 50.7%, fair -103. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 37.9% vs 37.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Daniel Jones 200+ passing yds (62%) + Javonte Williams 60+ rushing yds (62%) + Jonathan Taylor 10+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 26.9%, fair +272. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.4% vs 17.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Javonte Williams 30+ rushing yds (91%) + Keenan Allen 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 82.9%, fair -486. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.6% vs 76.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Dak Prescott 200+ passing yds (80%) + Josh Downs 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Keenan Allen 20+ receiving yds (79%). Joint estimate 50.7%, fair -103. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 37.9% vs 37.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Daniel Jones 200+ passing yds (62%) + Javonte Williams 60+ rushing yds (62%) + Jonathan Taylor 10+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 26.9%, fair +272. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.4% vs 17.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Confirm the starting QBs: Geno Smith and Patrick Mahomes. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  3. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  4. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Rashee Rice 15+ receiving yds (90%) + Patrick Mahomes 160+ passing yds (89%). Joint estimate 83.4%, fair -502. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.0% vs 72.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Patrick Mahomes 190+ passing yds (79%) + Xavier Worthy 15+ receiving yds (78%) + Breece Hall 15+ rushing yds (78%). Joint estimate 51.7%, fair -107. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.2% vs 37.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Braelon Allen 35+ rushing yds (61%) + Patrick Mahomes 230+ passing yds (60%) + Kenneth Walker III 10+ receiving yds (59%). Joint estimate 23.9%, fair +318. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.0% vs 16.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Rashee Rice 15+ receiving yds (90%) + Patrick Mahomes 160+ passing yds (89%). Joint estimate 83.4%, fair -502. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.0% vs 72.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Patrick Mahomes 190+ passing yds (79%) + Xavier Worthy 15+ receiving yds (78%) + Breece Hall 15+ rushing yds (78%). Joint estimate 51.7%, fair -107. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.2% vs 37.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Braelon Allen 35+ rushing yds (61%) + Patrick Mahomes 230+ passing yds (60%) + Kenneth Walker III 10+ receiving yds (59%). Joint estimate 23.9%, fair +318. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.0% vs 16.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Confirm the starting QBs: Jared Goff and Malik Willis. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  3. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  4. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Jameson Williams 10+ receiving yds (93%) + Malik Washington 10+ receiving yds (93%). Joint estimate 86.4%, fair -637. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 79.6% vs 79.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Jahmyr Gibbs 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Malik Willis 170+ passing yds (79%) + Greg Dulcich 20+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.1%, fair -118. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.2% vs 36.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jared Goff 260+ passing yds (60%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 70+ receiving yds (59%) + Jahmyr Gibbs 80+ rushing yds (59%). Joint estimate 29.0%, fair +245. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.2% vs 13.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Jameson Williams 10+ receiving yds (93%) + Malik Washington 10+ receiving yds (93%). Joint estimate 86.4%, fair -637. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 79.6% vs 79.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Jahmyr Gibbs 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Malik Willis 170+ passing yds (79%) + Greg Dulcich 20+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.1%, fair -118. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.2% vs 36.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jared Goff 260+ passing yds (60%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 70+ receiving yds (59%) + Jahmyr Gibbs 80+ rushing yds (59%). Joint estimate 29.0%, fair +245. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.2% vs 13.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

  2. Confirm the starting QBs: Shedeur Sanders and Tyler Shough. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  3. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  4. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Quinshon Judkins 20+ rushing yds (94%) + Chris Olave 25+ receiving yds (88%). Joint estimate 82.7%, fair -477. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.8% vs 75.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Tyler Shough 170+ passing yds (76%) + Quinshon Judkins 40+ rushing yds (75%) + Chris Olave 40+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 49.8%, fair +101. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 37.6% vs 32.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Juwan Johnson 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Alvin Kamara 20+ rushing yds (58%) + Tyler Shough 200+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 24.4%, fair +310. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.3% vs 15.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Confirm the starting QBs: J.J. McCarthy and Tanner McKee. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  3. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  4. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Malik Nabers 25+ receiving yds (94%) + Isaiah Likely 15+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 85.8%, fair -605. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 78.8% vs 78.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Malik Nabers 50+ receiving yds (78%) + Malachi Fields 10+ receiving yds (77%) + J.J. McCarthy 180+ passing yds (76%). Joint estimate 56.8%, fair -132. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 44.4% vs 35.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Malachi Fields 20+ receiving yds (61%) + Theo Johnson 10+ receiving yds (60%) + Malik Nabers 70+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 22.1%, fair +353. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 15.7% vs 15.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Malik Nabers 25+ receiving yds (94%) + Isaiah Likely 15+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 85.8%, fair -605. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 78.8% vs 78.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Malik Nabers 50+ receiving yds (78%) + Malachi Fields 10+ receiving yds (77%) + J.J. McCarthy 180+ passing yds (76%). Joint estimate 56.8%, fair -132. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 44.4% vs 35.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Malachi Fields 20+ receiving yds (61%) + Theo Johnson 10+ receiving yds (60%) + Malik Nabers 70+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 22.1%, fair +353. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 15.7% vs 15.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Confirm the starting QBs: Matthew Stafford and Jayden Daniels. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  3. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  4. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Matthew Stafford 160+ passing yds (92%) + Puka Nacua 40+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 87.6%, fair -705. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 80.2% vs 77.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Matthew Stafford 200+ passing yds (79%) + Puka Nacua 60+ receiving yds (79%) + Kyren Williams 10+ receiving yds (74%). Joint estimate 54.7%, fair -121. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 42.9% vs 36.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Matthew Stafford 240+ passing yds (59%) + Colby Parkinson 15+ receiving yds (55%) + Tutu Atwell 10+ receiving yds (55%). Joint estimate 23.3%, fair +330. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.9% vs 13.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Balanced: Matthew Stafford 200+ passing yds (79%) + Puka Nacua 60+ receiving yds (79%) + Kyren Williams 10+ receiving yds (74%). Joint estimate 54.7%, fair -121. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 42.9% vs 36.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Confirm the starting QBs: Bo Nix and Bryce Young. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  3. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  4. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Tetairoa McMillan 15+ receiving yds (95%) + Chuba Hubbard 30+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 87.9%, fair -724. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 83.3% vs 83.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Bryce Young 180+ passing yds (80%) + Courtland Sutton 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Bo Nix 150+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.3%, fair -119. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.8% vs 37.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Marvin Mims Jr. 10+ receiving yds (60%) + Bo Nix 180+ passing yds (59%) + Troy Franklin 10+ receiving yds (57%). Joint estimate 27.1%, fair +269. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.0% vs 15.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Tetairoa McMillan 15+ receiving yds (95%) + Chuba Hubbard 30+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 87.9%, fair -724. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 83.3% vs 83.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Bryce Young 180+ passing yds (80%) + Courtland Sutton 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Bo Nix 150+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.3%, fair -119. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.8% vs 37.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Marvin Mims Jr. 10+ receiving yds (60%) + Bo Nix 180+ passing yds (59%) + Troy Franklin 10+ receiving yds (57%). Joint estimate 27.1%, fair +269. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.0% vs 15.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Brenen Thompson (WR, Doubtful).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: C.J. Stroud and Justin Herbert. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Dalton Schultz 10+ receiving yds (86%) + Nico Collins 20+ receiving yds (82%). Joint estimate 70.1%, fair -234. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 58.8% vs 58.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: C.J. Stroud 170+ passing yds (80%) + Justin Herbert 150+ passing yds (80%) + Dalton Schultz 15+ receiving yds (79%). Joint estimate 55.0%, fair -122. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 42.5% vs 38.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tre Harris 15+ receiving yds (62%) + Justin Herbert 180+ passing yds (61%) + Nico Collins 40+ receiving yds (59%). Joint estimate 26.6%, fair +276. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.4% vs 15.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Keisean Nixon (CB, Questionable), Hunter Henry (TE, Questionable), Mack Hollins (WR, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Jordan Love and Drake Maye. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Drake Maye 150+ passing yds (90%) + DeMario Douglas 10+ receiving yds (90%). Joint estimate 83.5%, fair -505. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.3% vs 73.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Drake Maye 180+ passing yds (79%) + DeMario Douglas 20+ receiving yds (79%) + Jordan Love 190+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.2%, fair -118. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.7% vs 36.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jordan Love 220+ passing yds (61%) + Tucker Kraft 25+ receiving yds (60%) + Drake Maye 220+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 26.6%, fair +276. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.9% vs 14.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Drake Maye 150+ passing yds (90%) + DeMario Douglas 10+ receiving yds (90%). Joint estimate 83.5%, fair -505. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.3% vs 73.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Drake Maye 180+ passing yds (79%) + DeMario Douglas 20+ receiving yds (79%) + Jordan Love 190+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.2%, fair -118. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.7% vs 36.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jordan Love 220+ passing yds (61%) + Tucker Kraft 25+ receiving yds (60%) + Drake Maye 220+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 26.6%, fair +276. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 17.9% vs 14.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

  • LV gives up 61 yds/game to WR2 (league 41).
  • Run lane: Inside (middle / guard) gains 4.6 YPC on LV (league 3.8).
  • Run lane: Outside (tackle / end) gains 5.9 YPC on LV (league 4.6).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Darien Porter (CB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Kirk Cousins and Brock Purdy. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Kirk Cousins 160+ passing yds (91%) + Christian McCaffrey 20+ rushing yds (90%). Joint estimate 81.8%, fair -449. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.0% vs 76.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Christian McCaffrey 30+ rushing yds (79%) + Michael Mayer 10+ receiving yds (77%) + Ashton Jeanty 15+ receiving yds (76%). Joint estimate 45.9%, fair +118. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.2% vs 36.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Ashton Jeanty 25+ receiving yds (60%) + Jack Bech 10+ receiving yds (60%) + Kirk Cousins 230+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 28.9%, fair +246. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.0% vs 14.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Kirk Cousins 160+ passing yds (91%) + Christian McCaffrey 20+ rushing yds (90%). Joint estimate 81.8%, fair -449. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.0% vs 76.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Christian McCaffrey 30+ rushing yds (79%) + Michael Mayer 10+ receiving yds (77%) + Ashton Jeanty 15+ receiving yds (76%). Joint estimate 45.9%, fair +118. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.2% vs 36.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Ashton Jeanty 25+ receiving yds (60%) + Jack Bech 10+ receiving yds (60%) + Kirk Cousins 230+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 28.9%, fair +246. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.0% vs 14.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Jeremiyah Love (ankle) went on IR Nov 3, James Conner (foot, IR) won't return this week, and Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Thursday and is questionable (ESPN, citing Darren Urban). Tyler Allgeier's share should grow, so Arizona rushing lines are held out.

Lock was limited all week with a right elbow injury and is listed questionable, so if he can't go Milroe makes his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Isaiah Adams (G, Questionable), Walter Nolen III (DT, Questionable), Max Melton (CB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Gardner Minshew and Drew Lock. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

SEA strengths: explosive passing on defense (#2); explosive runs on defense (#2); success rate on defense (#2); 3rd downs on defense (#4); passing EPA on defense (#4). Weaknesses: red-zone TDs on defense (#28); rushing EPA on offense (#27).

Jeremiyah Love (ankle) went on IR Nov 3, James Conner (foot, IR) won't return this week, and Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Thursday and is questionable (ESPN, citing Darren Urban). Tyler Allgeier's share should grow, so Arizona rushing lines are held out.

Sam Darnold (quad) is ruled out; coach Mike Macdonald said the plan is for Drew Lock to start, with Jalen Milroe as backup (ESPN injury page; Spokesman-Review/NBC Sports, Nov 4-5). Lock was limited all week with a right elbow injury and is listed questionable, so if he can't go Milroe makes his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Isaiah Adams (G, Questionable); Jon Gaines II (G, Out); Jayden Williams (OT, Out); Walter Nolen III (DT, Questionable); Max Melton (CB, Questionable); Sam Darnold (QB, Out); Charles Cross (OT, Out); Brandon Pili (DT, Out); Uchenna Nwosu (LB, Out); Leonard Williams (DT, Out).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Emeka Egbuka (WR, Questionable), Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (CB, Questionable), Malik Muhammad II (CB, Questionable), Kyle Monangai (RB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Baker Mayfield and Caleb Williams. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Rome Odunze 10+ receiving yds (93%) + Luther Burden III 15+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 84.9%, fair -560. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.5% vs 77.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Rome Odunze 25+ receiving yds (80%) + Luther Burden III 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Caleb Williams 190+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 59.6%, fair -148. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 44.4% vs 36.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Kenny Gainwell 20+ rushing yds (61%) + Kalif Raymond 15+ receiving yds (60%) + D'Andre Swift 40+ rushing yds (60%). Joint estimate 21.9%, fair +357. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 16.4% vs 16.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Rome Odunze 10+ receiving yds (93%) + Luther Burden III 15+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 84.9%, fair -560. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.5% vs 77.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Rome Odunze 25+ receiving yds (80%) + Luther Burden III 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Caleb Williams 190+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 59.6%, fair -148. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 44.4% vs 36.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Kenny Gainwell 20+ rushing yds (61%) + Kalif Raymond 15+ receiving yds (60%) + D'Andre Swift 40+ rushing yds (60%). Joint estimate 21.9%, fair +357. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 16.4% vs 16.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.
